translations.answer: In the Jazzy/4.38.0/UR environment, the author confirmed that switching RMW_IMPLEMENTATION from rmw_zenoh_cpp to rmw_fastrtps_cpp eliminated the phenomenon; it was reproducible on Zenoh 0.2.8 deb and 0.2.9 commit 858f7b5. Switching RMW can be used as an isolation method, but the cause of delay in the service/publish path in Zenoh is not identified, and Cyclone DDS is not provided in the post.
translations.applicability: Ubuntu 24.04 PREEMPT_RT, ROS 2 Jazzy, controller_manager 4.38.0, UR 500 Hz with rmw_zenoh 0.2.8/0.2.9.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent reproduction is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author provided evidence of service calls, rqt, and system load; the maintainer measured the mutex region to be approximately 20 us.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author switched from rmw_zenoh to rmw_fastrtps and reproduced the issue on two Zenoh versions.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Fixing the ros2_control/controller_manager version, switching only RMW_IMPLEMENTATION for A/B.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Comparing controller_manager.total_time before, during, and after the service call; the maintainer did not reproduce it on the same version locally, indicating it is not solely a controller_manager version issue.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Temporarily switching from rmw_zenoh to Fast DDS in this environment; the author also plans to use Cyclone DDS.
translations.details.environments.0: Ubuntu 24.04; kernel 6.8.1-1037-realtime PREEMPT_RT; ROS 2 Jazzy; ros-jazzy-controller-manager 4.38.0-1noble.20251008.000820; rmw_zenoh 0.2.8 deb and 0.2.9 commit 858f7b5; Intel i7-11700.
translations.details.limits.0: Cannot conclude that all rmw_zenoh versions or all service calls have this issue.
translations.details.limits.1: Cyclone DDS does not provide actual test data on this thread; it is only a plan by the author.
translations.details.limits.2: The stale issue closure does not equal the root cause of Zenoh.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author confirmed that switching RMW alone eliminates the phenomenon; the root cause is not fully identified, and the issue was closed due to stale closure.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How can one narrow down the issue to the RMW layer when calling the controller_manager service during a 500 Hz control loop overrun and UR RTDE disconnection?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: RMW switching should be validated on an experimental platform before restoring to real machine high-speed operation.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The author confirmed the phenomenon occurs with rmw_zenoh, disappears when switching to Fast DDS; the internal lock and mechanism in Zenoh are not further identified.
translations.details.symptoms.0: List_controllers is called once per second, causing an update delay of approximately 3.16 ms and a total cycle of approximately 3.33 ms, missing the 500 Hz deadline.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Frequent calls lead to UR RTDE Data Pipeline overflow and disconnection.
translations.source.locator: ros2_control #2808 comment 3541490499, 3541707255; maintainer did not reproduce see 3541065379/3541219103
translations.source.title: ros2_control service call latency in the case is eliminated by switching RMW in this scenario, but root cause remains unknown.
translations.terms.0: Robot Operating System (ROS) middleware implementation (RMW) (机器人操作系统中间件实现)
translations.terms.2: Real-Time Data Exchange (RTDE) (实时数据交换)
translations.title: What is the temporary workaround validated by the original author for the service call triggering 500 Hz overrun in this case, and what root causes remain unknown?
